cdp.name: CDP
cdp.gloss: Customer Data Platform — the unified store of who your customers are.

perso.name: Personalization (1:1)
perso.gloss: Tailoring the message to the individual, not the segment.

genai.name: Generative AI
genai.gloss: Models that produce content — copy, images, replies — from a prompt.

agentic.name: Agentic AI
agentic.gloss: Systems that don't just generate, they decide and act toward a goal.

decis.name: Agentic decisioning
decis.gloss: An agent choosing what to say, when, how often and on which channel — per person.

bandit.name: Bandits / RL
bandit.gloss: The maths that lets a system learn which choice wins by trying and measuring.

cep.name: CEP
cep.gloss: Customer Engagement Platform — where this messaging actually runs.

geo.name: GEO
geo.gloss: Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers.

govern.name: Governance
govern.gloss: The controls that make automated decisions safe, explainable and legible.

stories.head: Pega's Peter van der Putten: AI governance needs more than one rulebook
stories.plain: Pega's AI Lab director explains why a single policy document isn't enough when automated systems are making next-best-action decisions and running agentic workflows. He argues governance must be baked into the model logic itself, not bolted on after. Critical reading for anyone buying or building AI that touches customer decisions at scale.

stories.head: Attentive's new CEO Eric Miao unveils individualized marketing vision and MCP general availability
stories.plain: Attentive is repositioning from SMS-first tool to full-lifecycle omnichannel platform, and shipping MCP (Model Context Protocol) general availability so OpenAI and Anthropic tools can plug directly into Attentive data and workflows. That's a structural shift in how third-party AI agents can act on customer data inside a CEP — worth watching for buyers and builders alike.

stories.head: SOCi report: What actually drives local AI visibility for multi-location brands
stories.plain: SOCi's research breaks down which signals — reviews, local pages, structured data — most influence whether a multi-location brand surfaces inside AI-generated answers. As consumers increasingly skip search and ask AI directly, generative engine optimization at the local level is becoming a budget-line decision for franchise and retail marketers.

stories.head: Twilio: 86% of firms rate AI customer service satisfactory; Attentive and PubMatic push agentic marketing
stories.plain: A Twilio survey finds most businesses are satisfied with AI-assisted service, but only half of consumers agree — a gap that matters for trust and adoption. Separately, both Attentive and PubMatic announced agentic marketing capabilities, signalling that autonomous campaign execution is moving from pilot to product across the industry.

stories.head: How to combine Marketing Mix Modeling with post-purchase survey attribution
stories.plain: Practical guide showing how enterprise teams layer top-down MMM statistics with bottom-up survey data to capture dark social and offline word-of-mouth that neither method catches alone. As AI-driven spend decisions rely on clean attribution inputs, getting measurement right upstream is foundational — making this a workflow staple, not just methodology theory.

stories.head: Pega's Peter van der Putten on why AI governance needs more than one rulebook
stories.plain: Pega's AI Lab director explains why a single governance policy can't cover both next-best-action models and agentic workflows — they carry different risks and need different controls. As more brands hand decisions to autonomous systems, understanding how to structure layered AI governance is essential for anyone buying or building marketing AI.

stories.head: Attentive's new CEO Eric Miao unveils individualized marketing vision and MCP general availability
stories.plain: Attentive is shipping Model Context Protocol (MCP) general availability, letting OpenAI and Anthropic tools plug directly into Attentive customer data and campaign workflows. This is a concrete infrastructure move — not a vision statement — that changes how agentic marketing tools can access and act on first-party data inside a major omnichannel engagement platform.

stories.head: AI traffic drives 83% more revenue per visit, Adobe research finds
stories.plain: Adobe's data shows visitors arriving from AI-generated answers convert 90% better and generate 83% more revenue per session than average web traffic. This is the clearest commercial evidence yet that brands must actively pursue Generative Engine Optimization — being visible inside AI answers is becoming a revenue-critical channel.

stories.head: Usercentrics CEO: 52% of consumers will pay a 7% premium for AI data transparency
stories.plain: New Usercentrics research shows consumers are willing to pay more when brands are clear about how AI uses their data, putting a measurable price tag on consent and transparency. The finding reframes data governance from a compliance cost into a revenue lever — and suggests consent rates belong in media planning, not just legal review.

stories.head: ChatGPT paid traffic worth 64% less per session than paid Google Search
stories.plain: Paid visits via ChatGPT generated only 89 cents revenue per session versus $2.45 from Google paid search. For marketers allocating budget across AI and traditional search channels, this benchmark rebalances the hype: AI-driven discovery traffic is growing but its commercial conversion quality still lags Google significantly.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Answer Engines Are the New Discovery Layer
body: ChatGPT and Claude are now live commercial surfaces — URLgenius is already routing holiday shoppers through app links embedded in those chats, while SOCi data shows AI answer engines reshaping local brand visibility. The search funnel is bifurcating: Google still converts paid clicks at higher revenue-per-visit, but AI referral traffic delivers 83% more revenue per organic visit, forcing marketers to optimise for two very different discovery logics simultaneously.

This shift is not incremental. Brands that fail to engineer their content, structured data, & local signals for AI retrieval risk being invisible in the channel that is growing fastest. The strategic decision is no longer whether to invest in AI search optimisation but how to allocate budget between legacy SEM and emerging AI-answer placement before the gap in audience share widens further.

themes.head: Consent & Transparency as a Pricing Signal
body: Usercentrics CEO Donna Dror's finding that 52% of consumers will pay more for brands with clear data practices reframes privacy compliance as a revenue lever, not a cost centre. The MarTech piece on engineering consent beyond the checkbox reinforces the same point: opt-in architecture is now a brand differentiator that shows up in willingness-to-pay, not just legal audits.

For martech buyers this means data-transparency tooling belongs on the same roadmap as personalisation engines — the two are linked because trust is the prerequisite for the data quality that makes AI personalisation work. Brands that treat consent as a surface-level checkbox will progressively lose share to those that make transparency a product feature.

themes.head: Measurement Is Fragmenting Beyond Attribution
body: Three separate pieces in the past 30 days converge on the same structural problem: no single attribution model tells the full story anymore. Combining Marketing Mix Modelling with post-purchase surveys, extending B2B CTV beyond brand metrics, and tracking multi-screen behaviour during high-stakes events all point to a world where measurement must be layered and method-diverse rather than unified through one dashboard.

The practical implication is that marketing teams need to stop searching for a single source of truth and instead design a portfolio of measurement methods — each calibrated to the decision it informs. Buying a new martech platform without first auditing your measurement context (as the Nov 4 MarTech guide advises) now represents a material budget risk.

themes.head: AI Productivity Gains Still Need a CFO Argument
body: AI tools are visibly accelerating content velocity — Adobe's creative AI report, Templafy's document agents, and Wizstar's low-cost video generation model all document speed and cost improvements. But speed alone does not convert to ROI unless the time saved is redirected into higher-value work and tracked against a revenue baseline, which most teams have not yet established.

The MarTech analysis on AI complicating marketing centralisation adds a structural wrinkle: AI proliferation is creating shadow tool sprawl across teams, undermining the stack consolidation that CMOs spent the previous decade pursuing. The governance challenge is now as large as the capability opportunity, and both require a deliberate operating model — not just a tool policy.

themes.head: Hyper-Local & Contextual Targeting Goes Granular
body: Inuvo pushing CTV intent signals to the neighbourhood level and SOCi mapping AI visibility drivers for multi-location brands both signal the same directional move: the targeting unit is shrinking from DMA to block level. This is enabled by AI models that can infer contextual intent without relying on third-party cookies, making hyper-local precision more achievable at scale than it has ever been.

For multi-location brands and B2B advertisers running CTV, this represents a genuine capability unlock — but it also raises the bar on creative localisation, since a neighbourhood-level signal paired with generic creative wastes the precision advantage. The workflow bottleneck shifts from data to content production, which is exactly why automated listing tools like ListEasier and AI video generation are emerging in parallel.

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — discovery, measurement, content, targeting, & consent — AI is forcing marketers to rebuild operating models rather than simply add new tools to existing ones.
